answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the sonnet schedule in the knoll ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the haven checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 5 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 146 aliases therefore means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. That is 31 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
